name: pgrep
description: Finds processes by name or attributes and prints their PIDs — grep for the process table, without the grep-itself problem.

flags.description: Prints matching PIDs, one per line.
Match against the full command line, not just the program name.

examples.explanation: PIDs of the nginx master and workers.
Shows the full command line, confirming exactly which script is running.
-f matches the whole command line, distinguishing this instance from other python processes.
The classic pairing: kill every PID that pgrep finds.

about: pgrep matches by extended regex against the process name (15 chars by default) unless -f is given. It never matches itself — the main advantage over ps aux | grep x | grep -v grep. Its sibling pkill sends signals to matches directly.
useCases: Check whether a service process is running.
Find processes by full command line.
mistakes: Expecting pgrep to match long command lines without -f.
Forgetting that names are truncated to 15 characters without -f.
